title: Why the Bears GM Shouted Out My Book
author: David Epstein
summary: David Epstein reports that Chicago Bears general manager Ryan Poles cited his book Inside the Box to explain how injury constraints pushed the defence to invent new ways of pressuring quarterbacks. Epstein ties this to an NBA study of nearly thirty thousand games, which found that when a star was sidelined, teammates spread the ball more and kept doing so afterward, improving results. He distils the value of constraints into two effects: they force leaders to clarify priorities and push teams into productive experimentation. The practical advice is to deny yourself the most familiar tool or process and see what you build around it. He applies the same discipline to his own writing.
points: Bears GM Ryan Poles credited injury-driven constraints with forcing a broader, more creative defensive toolbox.
An NBA study of about thirty thousand games showed teams improved when forced to stop relying on a single star.
Epstein boils the value of constraints down to clarifying priorities and forcing productive experimentation.
Leaders can try it by blocking their most familiar solution and seeing what emerges.
Epstein discarded his first instinct to open each chapter, a deliberate desirable difficulty.
